questions.q: Why can't you just query mid-flight data flow rows the way you'd query a table?
options: Rows are streaming through in-memory buffers, not sitting in a queryable location
SSIS encrypts all data flow rows by default
SQL Server locks the data flow engine during execution
Data flow rows only exist after the package finishes running
questions.explain: The data flow engine moves rows through memory buffers in batches for performance — there's no table to SELECT from mid-flight, which is exactly the gap a Data Viewer fills.

questions.q: What does a Data Viewer attach to?
options: A path — the connector between two data flow components
An entire package
A connection manager
The Control Flow tab
questions.explain: Data Viewers are configured per-path via the Data Flow Path Editor, so you can watch exactly the data moving between two specific components.

questions.q: What happens to package execution the moment a Data Viewer's buffer is ready to display?
options: Execution pauses until you click Continue (the green arrow)
The package fails immediately
Nothing — execution continues at full speed regardless
The buffer is automatically logged to a file and execution continues
questions.explain: An attached Data Viewer pauses the data flow at each buffer, waiting for you to advance — this pause is exactly why Data Viewers must never be left on in a production package.

questions.q: What does clicking Detach do to an active Data Viewer?
options: Stops pausing execution and stops updating the viewer's display, while data keeps flowing
Permanently deletes the Data Viewer from the path
Immediately stops the entire package
Copies the current buffer to the clipboard
questions.explain: Detach lets the data flow resume at full speed without the viewer's pause-and-display behavior — the viewer is still there, just not actively pausing execution, unlike Copy Data which just grabs the current buffer's contents.

questions.q: Why should Data Viewers always be removed or disabled before deploying a package to production?
options: An active Data Viewer pauses the data flow waiting for a human to click Continue — in an unattended scheduled run, the package would simply hang
Data Viewers corrupt data as it passes through
SQL Server Agent jobs cannot execute packages containing Data Viewers at all
Data Viewers permanently slow down all future executions, even after removal
questions.explain: Data Viewers are a development-time debugging aid — the pause-and-wait behavior that makes them useful while building a package would make a scheduled, unattended production run hang indefinitely.
